episodes.162716: Showers and thunderstorms developed along and ahead of a strong cold front and produced a waterspout and a marine thunderstorm wind gust.
episodes.162819: Showers and thunderstorms developed along and ahead of a strong cold front and produced funnel clouds, wind damage and a tornado.
episodes.162933: A very potent upper level trough entered the Southern Plains late on October 26th and ejected eastward into the Four-State Region on October 27th, accompanied by a strong cold front. A line of severe thunderstorms developed ahead of the cold front as the upper trough pivoted directly across the area. These storms resulted in numerous wind damage reports across parts of East and Deep East Texas throughout the morning hours before the line pushed east of the state line into western Louisiana by around midday.
episodes.162939: A very potent upper level trough entered the Southern Plains late on October 26th and ejected eastward into the Four-State Region on October 27th, accompanied by a strong cold front. A line of severe thunderstorms developed ahead of the cold front as the upper trough pivoted directly across the area. These storms resulted in numerous reports of wind damage across parts of East Texas throughout the morning hours before the line pushed east into North Louisiana around midday through the mid-afternoon hours.
episodes.163149: Thunderstorms developed into eastern Oklahoma during the early morning hours of the 27th. The strongest storm produced severe wind gusts up to 64 mph.
episodes.163211: A strong upper level storm system moving across northern New Mexico on the 26th brought severe thunderstorms to the Rolling Plains as moisture surged northward east of a dryline. As lift from the approaching system increased, storms rapidly developed along the dryline Tuesday evening across the central and eastern Rolling Plains. Strong wind shear and decent instability caused several of these storms to become severe as they rapidly evolved into a line. Ping pong ball sized hail was reported in rural Kent County. Even more impressive, a wind gust of 96 mph was measured by the Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet near Hackberry (Cottle County) as the storms moved through.
episodes.163386: A line of storms moved out of southwest Kansas into the central sections producing strong winds up to 50 mph at many locations.  However, one very localized area produced a brief QLCS tornado.
episodes.163479: A dryline and strong upper trough combined to produce numerous thunderstorms during the evening and overnight period of the 26th into the 27th. Storms produced isolated extreme wind gusts early in the event, with sporadic wind damage and a tornado then reported in central Oklahoma.
episodes.163546: A cold front moved through the region during the afternoon hours of October 27th. Ahead of this front, showers and thunderstorms developed mainly along and south of the I-20 corridor. A tornado occurred in far southern Concordia Parish.
episodes.163578: Thunderstorms erupted along a dryline over the Big Country and produced damaging wind gusts as they moved east across North and Central Texas during the overnight hours of Tuesday, October 26th, into Wednesday, October 27th.
episodes.163584: A low pressure nor'easter underwent bombogenesis as it developed east of Nantucket on the 26th.  It then moved west toward Nantucket Sound, before heading eastward again back out to sea on the 27th.  Winds gusted to 60-90+ mph.  More than one-half million power outages were reported...495,000 in MA and 96,800 in RI. Schools were closed for multiple days, as it took a while to clean up the downed trees/wires and to restore power.
episodes.163609: Throughout the day, a cold front gradually moved into Northwest Kansas. As the front crossed the Colorado border, strong winds spread a fire near the town of Ruleton damaging a railroad track, power pole, and a patch of farmland. During the early evening hours, a line of thunderstorms developed along the cold front as it moved east of U.S. Highway 83. The line of storms produced up to 70 mph wind gusts in Hill City and up to nickel sized hail across Gove, Sheridan, Decatur, and Graham counties.
episodes.163610: During the early evening hours, a line of thunderstorms developed along a cold front as it moved along and east of U.S. Highway 83. The storms produced pea to nickel sized hail near the city of McCook.
episodes.163626: Thunderstorms developed along a cold front that moved into a conditionally unstable airmass with strong vertical wind shear. Some of these storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.163765: Initiation of thunderstorms near the Hwy 283 corridor formed into a mainly linear line along the dryline.
episodes.163793: A line of thunderstorms moved through the coastal waters of the northern Coastal Bend during the morning of the 27th. Storms produced wind gusts from 35 to 40 knots.
episodes.163828: A coastal storm brought a prolonged period of moderate rainfall across portions of eastern New York, mainly on Tuesday, October 26, 2021. While the rain was not falling particularly heavily, persistent rainfall rates of 0.25 to 0.50 of an inch an hour occurred for several hours across portions of Ulster, Greene, Schoharie and Schenectady counties. This resulted in rainfall amounts of 2 to 5 inches across the region. Minor flooding began as early as the late morning hours on October 26, but the greatest coverage of flooding occurred during the afternoon and evening hours as roads began to close. Rivers, creeks and streams also began overflowing their banks leading to additional flooding. Rain ended during the overnight hours, slowly allowing waters to recede. However, roads damaged by the flooding remained closed into the daytime hours of October 27.||Gusty winds between 30 and 40 mph also accompanied the storm which resulted in a few downed trees and some power outages.||New York Governor Kathy Hochul declared a State of Emergency for selected counties across New York State including Greene, Montgomery, Schenectady, Schoharie and Ulster.
episodes.163831: A dryline and strong upper trough combined to produce numerous thunderstorms during the evening and overnight period of the 26th into the 27th. Storms produced isolated severe wind gusts across portions of western north Texas.
episodes.163875: A vigorous storm system moved through Southeast Texas spawning tornadoes and severe weather.
episodes.163876: A vigorous system moved through the region during the 27th spawning a few tornadoes and severe thunderstorms.
episodes.163877: A thunderstorm moved across Sabine Pass producing a high wind gust.
episodes.163947: A line of strong thunderstorms moved across the marine area and produced gusty winds.
episodes.163970: A warm front lifted north across the local area during the morning hours. This brought in a surge of warm and moist air. At the same time, mid level temperatures were dropping. That combination dramatically increased instability across the region. A line of thunderstorms and discrete cells ahead of the cold front developed and produced a few tornadoes, flash flooding, and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.163971: A warm front lifted north across the local area during the morning hours. This brought in a surge of warm and moist air. At the same time, mid level temperatures were dropping. That combination dramatically increased instability across the region. A line of thunderstorms and discrete cells ahead of the cold front developed and produced a few tornadoes, flash flooding, and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.163972: A warm front lifted north across the local area during the morning hours. This brought in a surge of warm and moist air. At the same time, mid level temperatures were dropping. That combination dramatically increased instability across the region. A line of thunderstorms and discrete cells ahead of the cold front developed and produced a few tornadoes, flash flooding, and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.164005: The combination of an upper level disturbance and weak instability caused scattered thunderstorms to develop. a few storms were severe.
episodes.164032: An upper level closed low meandered through the Great Lakes while slowly phasing with an Atlantic Nor'easter. Convergence along an inverted trough coincided with a strong push of Atlantic moisture to force periods of heavy rainfall south of Lake Ontario from Rochester eastward through the latter half of the day.
episodes.164070: A strong low pressure system moved from the Ohio Valley to the East Coast and reformed as a powerful nor'easter while moving into New England. This provided the region with several hours of moderate to heavy rainfall. In addition to significant flash flooding around the area, widespread minor to moderate river flooding occurred on many of the larger, main stem rivers and their tributaries.

events.narrative: Over a duration of 10 minutes, hail ranging in size from pea to nickel in size at the location.
Dime to nickel sized hail reported.
Catskill Creek went over its banks causing minor flooding along West Main Street in the Village of Catskill.
Pea to nickel sized hail covered half the ground at the location. The spotter also noted the hail was bouncing at least 3 ft off the ground.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Guthrie measured a wind gust to 60 mph.
A storm chaser measured hail up to ping pong ball size along US Highway 380 in Kent County.
Pea to nickel sized hail reported.
A pivot irrigation sprinkler was overturned by the high wind.  There was also a large tree blown down and damage was done to a shed.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Hackberry measured severe wind gusts from 1942 CST through 1943 CST. A peak wind gust of 96 mph was measured at 1943 CST.
ASOS station KHLC at the Hill City Municipal Airport measured a 70 mph wind gust over a 5 minute span at 1945 and 1950.
A storm chaser near Leedey observed a tornado estimated to be about 8 miles west-northwest of Leedey (or about 16 miles east-northeast of Roll). No damage was reported.
Extensive lowland flooding was reported along the Irondequoit Creek between Ellison Park and Powder Mills Park.

The QLCS tornado touched down just outside of Turon, KS, and moved to the NNE across town.  The bulk of the damage was limited to trees as the tornado strength at the surface appeared to be much lower than that at tree top level.  A few homes and buildings were damaged as trees fell onto many roofs and some sheet metal was peeled off of a barn.  Some playground equipment was also blown over in the park close to where the tornado lifted. Winds were estimated to be around 80 mph with this tornado.
The Sterling City 4 WSW Mesonet recorded a wind gust of 61 mph.

Moderate flooding occurred on the Delaware River at Callicoon. The river crested at 13.68 feet at midnight on October 27th. Flood stage is 12 feet at this location. At 13 feet, flooding reaches the parking lot of the bank and the lower part of the gas station parking lot near the bridge in Callicoon.

Moderate flooding occurred on the Susquehanna River at Vestal. The river crested at 22.24 feet on October 27th at 6:30 AM. Flood stage at this location is 18 feet. At 22 feet, Moore Park in Vestal floods. Flooding to first floor level begins at the low ends of Davis Avenue, Shady Drive, Verdun Avenue and Fairmont in Endwell.
A weak tornado from a QLCS (Quasi-Linear Convective System) produced a brief, weak tornado that damaged trees and two barns on the south and southeast side of Union City.
A wind gust of 60 mph was recorded at the Abilene Regional Airport.

A tornado from a QLCS (quasi-linear convective system) storm developed in northeast Norman about a half mile northwest of 24th Avenue NE and Rock Creek Road, and moved generally northeast into southwest Oklahoma City dissipating northwest of SE 164th Street and Anderson Road. The damage was most intense from a half mile south to about a half mile east of the intersection of 36th Avenue NE and Franklin Road where the tornado produced roof damage to two barns, and damaged the soffit to a carport at a home. Otherwise, the tornado produced damage primarily to trees along the path.
A large oak tree was snapped about 3 feet above the ground south of 96th Avenue NE and Tecumseh Road.
A 64 mph wind gust was measured at Graham Municipal Airport.
A 61 mph wind gust was reported at a CWOP site 15 miles north of Jacksboro.
A 63 mph wind gust was measured at Mineral Wells Airport.
A report of broken 3-inch tree limbs and power poles was received via mPing.
A 62 mph wind gust was measured at the New Fairview CWOP station.

At a NDBC buoy 1 mile northeast of Chatham, a gust to 76 mph was recorded at 354 AM EDT (254 AM EST).  At a NDBC buoy 11 miles south of Hyannis, a gust to 67 mph was recorded at 420 AM EDT.  A NOS-NWLON site for Nantucket recorded a gust to 64 mph at 336 AM EDT.
An amateur radio operator measured a 61 mph wind gust at the intersection of US 380 and FM 156.
A 60 mph wind gusts was measured by a WeatherSTEM station at Texas Motor Speedway.
A 61 mph wind gust was estimated at Denton Municipal Airport.
At 411 AM EDT (311 AM EST) on the 27th, a Weatherflow mesonet site at Woods Hole measured a wind gust to 79 mph.

At 459 AM EDT (359 AM EST) on the 27th, a Weatherflow mesonet site at Dog Bar Breakwater off of Gloucester recorded a wind gust to 79 mph.  At 450 AM EDT (350 AM EST), a NDBC buoy located 11 miles NNE of Scituate recorded a wind gust to 65 mph.

Around daybreak, Weatherflow mesonet stations recorded the following peak gusts:  |77 mph at Deer Island (647 AM EDT or 547 AM EST); 71 mph at Squantum Point at 548 AM EDT; 66 mph at Pleasure Bay at 552 AM EDT; and 63 mph at Dread Ledge at 640 AM EDT.
The ASOS at the McAlester Regional Airport measured 64 mph thunderstorm wind gusts.

The following peak wind gusts were observed on Narragansett Bay.|80 mph at Castle Island at 704 AM EDT (604 AM EST) - Weatherflow.|72 mph at Borden Flats Light at 512 AM EDT - NOS-PORTS.|68 mph at Halfway Rock at 544 AM EDT - Weatherflow.|64 mph at Conimicut Light at 612 AM EDT - NOS-PORTS.|62 mph at Sabin Point at 706 AM EDT - Weatherflow.
A line of thunderstorms produced wind gusts estimated at 65 mph that uprooted a large tree and blew down fencing near Buttercup Creek Blvd. and Twin Oak Trl. in Cedar Creek.
A line of thunderstorms produced wind gusts estimated at 60 mph that caused minor damage to a roof and knocked down several large tree branches in northern Austin.
A line of thunderstorms produced wind gusts estimated at 70 mph. A broadcast media partner shared pictures on social media of a 10-12 inch diameter tree limb down near Newport Ave. in Austin.
A line of thunderstorms produced wind gusts estimated at 65 mph than uprooted a large tree near N. Shields Dr. and Kellies Farm Ln. in northern Austin.
At 6 AM EDT (5 AM EST) on the 27th, a NDBC buoy located 9 miles southeast of Little Compton measured a wind gust to 77 mph.
At 704 AM EDT (604 AM EST) on the 27th, a Weatherflow mesonet station at the tip of Point Judith recorded a wind gust to 77 mph.
Webcam caught circulation forming over Jones Bay.
Funnel cloud was observed near Bayou Vista on a webcam. There were no reports of damage.
Webcam showed well developed funnel looking northeast from Tiki Island. Feature heading out over Galveston Bay.
Minor flooding was observed on the Honeoye Creek at Honeoye Falls. The river level peaked at 6.6 feet.
Trees were down on a home in Pinehurst.
Trees were down at the Jersey Meadow Golf Course.
A large tree was down on a home on Airway Drive and caused significant damage. Other minor damage was found in the area that stretched about 100 yards long and about 30 yards wide.
There was a video showing a funnel cloud.

A brief EF-0 tornado was observed near Grand Oaks High School in Spring. Based on video, it appeared to briefly touch down in a field. A flipped over soccer goal was the only evident damage for the very short lived weak tornado.

A brief tornado started just west of Nick Ave in Port Acres where there was damage to out buildings and caused some roof damage to homes. The tornado moved northeast crossing Silver Ave then curved north northeast crossing 63 street before dissipating near 64th Street. Numerous limbs were blown down. Max estimated winds were 80 MPH.
Trees were down on Rosemary Lane.
Tree down on County Road 3397, FM 782 near County Road 2186, FM 225 2 miles north of Hwy 284, FM 2496 near County Road 3161 and State Hwy 42 northwest of Hwy 795.

A NWS Storm Survey determined that straight-line winds with estimated wind gusts up to 80 mph produced various wind damage in Downtown Lufkin. Sporadic damage was first observed near the Lufkin Police Station on East Shepherd Ave. where a small tree was toppled. As the wind pushed across South 4th Street, small and large branches were broken off of hardwood trees. A billboard on East Lufkin Ave. was destroyed and a few branches on trees were broken along K. Morgan Ave. ||Surveillance footage and emergency officials observed a narrow circulation at the ground which was determined to be a turbulent eddy that developed as the damaging winds came to the surface. The damage was determined to be non-tornadic as there was no evidence of vertical motion with the damage pattern oriented in a northeasterly direction. In addition, there was no evident funnel cloud from the footage shared that would indicate the circulation was vertically attached to rotation from the parent storm.
TCOON site as Seadrift measured a gust to 37 knots.

A tornado touched down south of Old Hwy 90 near the Hwy 62 exit on I-10, severely damaging a brick home. A large building in the backyard was destroyed, an RV was tossed 25 yards, a truck flipped over, and 3 other vehicles were pushed out of the driveway. An ATV stored in the building in the backyard was picked up by the tornado and tossed across I-10. Further to the north on Hwy 62 at the TX DOT office, large warehouses in the back had the overhead doors blown in. Max estimated winds were 130 MPH.
Large tree limbs and fences were down.
There was minor damage to a school building. Trees and fences were down in the area.

A large tornado began near Hwy 1130, flipping a double wide mobile home that was tied down. A woman inside was critically injured. Other homes along Hwy 1130 had trees fall on them, roofs ripped off, and wind blown debris damage. The tornado continued north on South Teal Road, blowing down trees. Along Hudnall Road, several homes and garages lost their roofs. The tornado turned a little to the northeast, and hit the Woodland Ridge Acres subdivision off of Hwy 87, blowing down more trees. Max estimated wind speed was 130 MPH. The tornado continued into Newton County.
This tornado crossed from Orange County into Newton County, damaging|several homes and garages in Hartburg. Max estimated wind speed was 130 MPH.

events.narrative: The wind gust occurred at the Matagorda Bay WeatherFlow site.
Tree reported down on County Road 175.
Tree reported down in the northwest part of the county near State Hwy 43.
A tornado touched down along and near Hwy 109 in western Beauregard Parish, snapping or uprooting several trees. Max estimated winds were 110 MPH.

events.county: Pensacola Bay Area Including Santa Rosa Sound
events.narrative: KNPA, within one mile of the coast, measured a 48 mph thunderstorm wind gust.
A spotter reported damage to Wright's BBQ on Main Street in Vidor.
A tree was downed near Financial Plaza just west of the Shreveport Regional Airport.

events.narrative: The radar indicated a tornado debris signature east of Hwy 12 in western Calcasieu Parish. This is a rural area with no roads where the radar signature was seen. No damage was seen on Hwy 12.

A tornado touched down west of Elliott Road and traveled east parallel to and south of Ham Reid Road causing significant structural damage to around a dozen homes and minor damage to several more in the neighborhood. Reports from Calcasieu sheriff indicated a woman was injured when a window was blown into their home. A second person suffered a deep laceration to the leg as a result of blowing debris. The tornado weakened as it crossed Lake street and lifted as it passed along Aberdeen Drive. Max estimated wind speed was 130 MPH.

The tornado began on Industrial Ave off of Hwy 14. Two large warehouse-sized buildings has sections of their roof and wall collapse. Damage continued on the other side of I-210, where some trees were snapped off of East Prien Lake Road. One person was injured when a window blew in. Max estimated winds were 105 MPH.
Street flooding was reported in Beaumont with some streets impassable.
Walgreens near Lake and West McNeese Streets sustained minor roof damage.
Trees and power lines were downed on Highway 71 northwest of Colfax.
A tree was blown down on LA 773.

A brief and weak EF-0 tornado moved along Hwy 15 where several large limbs were snapped in addition to trees uprooted. A Tornado Debris Signature (TDS) was noted from the Fort Polk (KPOE) radar. The beginning point of this tornado is uncertain due to road|accessibility issues.

NWS survey team found damage consistent with an EF-0 tornado. The Tornado moved onshore from Lake Pontchartrain and touched down just north of Mariners Blvd near North Causeway Blvd. It caused minor structural damage to a residential home, ripping off a tin roof. As the tornado tracked north, it damaged a small tree and tore off section of tin roofing from the Mariners Plaza. It then progressed northward, lifting just before reaching the intersection of East Causeway Approach and Monroe Street.
Washington Parish Sheriffs office reported street flooding on Highway 10 near Bogue Chitto Heights.
The Causeway Police Department relayed a video of a waterspout in Lake Ponchartrain on the north side of the Causeway about 1 mile south of Mandeville.

A brief EF-1 tornado touched down just west of Bales Ave in Picayune, MS. This tornado quickly traveled northeast, with widespread tree damage in the eastern part of the town. Many trees were snapped at the base with multiple tin roofs ripped off as well as minor structural damage. The worst damage was to two trailers just west of the highway. One was spun 180 degrees and flipped with extensive damage and another rolled 100 yards and was completely obliterated. The tornado crossed the highway with other straight line wind damage noted along the damage path on|the east side of the highway. The tornado seems to have lifted near Northwood drive where a small shed was destroyed along with minor structural damage and multiple trees and branches snapped. On both sides of the path there was|evidence of straight line wind damage which was consistent with radar at the time. The width that was estimated was due to a wider swath seen in the east part of the city. It was difficult to distinguish tornado vs. straight line wind at times.
A thunderstorm wind gust downed a large tree limb.
A storm survey indicated multiple trees down just east of I-59 and south of Sycamore road due to straight line damaging winds.
